title: Design systems: tokens, type scales and themes

videos.script:
Four lessons of this course are about delivery. The next four are about consistency. How a team makes forty screens look like one product, without anybody checking each pixel.

{{tokens}} It starts with tokens. A token is a design decision with a name. The green of a button, the size of a heading, the gap between two cards. Written down once, as data, and used everywhere by name.

{{generate}} The planner's tokens go in a JSON file, and a script of twenty lines turns them into CSS custom properties. You will read every line of it.

{{scale}} Then a type scale, where every size is the one before it times a ratio. And a spacing scale on a four pixel grid.

{{contrast}} Then colour, and the check that matters most. A second script measures every pair of text and background against the accessibility standard. You will watch it fail on a grey that looked fine.

{{themes}} And themes. A dark theme is not a second stylesheet. It is the same names pointing at different values.
